fixes.explanation: John 6:2 says a large crowd followed Him "…because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick." That's the reason the text gives. Signs on the sick, and the crowd followed. I think I'd have been right there with them, friend.

John 6:2 doesn't mention any leaders sending anybody. The reason it gives is that the crowd followed "…because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick." The signs are the reason on the page, and that's where I'll leave it.

John 6:6 says it plainly: "…He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." The question wasn't because Jesus was stuck. He already knew what He was about to do. I think Philip was in for a surprise.

Comfort is a kind guess, friend, but verse 6 doesn't go there. It says Jesus asked "…to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." Philip, one of His disciples, was being tested, and the text doesn't say he needed soothing. Me, I'd have wanted a hug and a cookie.

Philip says in John 6:7, "Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece." So his answer is no: that money wouldn't be enough. Philip, one of Jesus' disciples, ran the numbers, and he said they wouldn't cover it.

A small piece comes up in verse 7, where Philip, one of His disciples, says two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece. John 6:11 says Jesus distributed to those seated "…as much as they wanted." Then everyone was full, and there were leftovers on top of that.

The text doesn't give a portion like that. John 6:11 says Jesus distributed "…as much as they wanted." and verse 12 says everyone was full. Twelve baskets were left over from the five barley loaves (John 6:13).

Jesus says, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted." (John 6:12). Everybody's already full, and He still tells His disciples to gather what's left. They collect the pieces and fill twelve baskets.

The word in John 6:12 is a different one. Jesus tells His disciples, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted." Wasted is the word He uses, friend, and forgotten isn't in the verse.

After they see the sign, the people begin to say, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world." (John 6:14). They'd just seen Jesus distribute five barley loaves and two small fish to those seated as much as they wanted. I think that'd get my attention too. And there's more to come in this story.

Elijah is a good guess, friend, but John 6:14 doesn't go there. What the people begin to say is, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world." That's the title the text gives, right after they saw the sign Jesus had performed. Elijah's name never comes up in this passage.

Nice try, friend, but the crowd isn't the one being moved around here. John 6:15 says Jesus "…withdrew again to a mountain by Himself." The text doesn't mention Him sending anyone anywhere. Jesus is the one who moves in this verse.

That's right. The text says the disciples got into a boat and started across the sea, and "…Jesus had not yet gone out to them." (John 6:17). He wasn't in the boat when they set out. Back in verse 15, He had withdrawn to a mountain by Himself.

They're not calm at all. John 6:19 says they saw Jesus "…approaching the boat, walking on the sea…" and they were terrified. It was already dark, with a strong wind blowing. What Jesus says to them comes next, in verse 20.
Jesus speaks up: "It is I; do not be afraid." (John 6:20). He tells them who it is and tells them not to be afraid. That's what He says to men in a dark boat who were terrified.

Holding on tight is a fair instinct in a boat like that, friend. But John 6:20 says Jesus spoke up: "It is I; do not be afraid." He told them who was coming toward the boat and told them not to be afraid. Nothing in the verse says to keep quiet.

John 6:21 says, "Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." They were willing to take Him in, and the boat reached the shore at once. After all that rowing, I'd call that a nice finish.

The boat keeps going the way it was headed. John 6:21 says they were willing to take Jesus into the boat, "…and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." Back in verse 17, they had started across the sea to Capernaum. The boat reached the shore where they were heading.
